highlightAliases.old: Stage 3: full-thickness, fat visible, no bone/muscle/tendon exposed (p686).
highlightAliases.new: Stage 3: full-thickness, fat visible, no bone/muscle/tendon exposed (p686-687, Figure 46-1).

highlightAliases.old: Saline/water lack antiseptic properties and should seldom be used on (colonized) PI — antiseptic options: Dakin's 0.25% or povidone-iodine (10%/1% free iodine) on colonized PI, applied 10–15 min before redressing; lavage 4–15 psi (p692). For clean wounds, less force and physiologic solutions such as normal saline can be used (p693); avoid antiseptics on clean and healing PI (p697).
highlightAliases.new: Clean a pressure injury with a nonirritating, nontoxic solution such as saline or clean water. Wound colonization alone does not justify routine antiseptics. If an antimicrobial cleanser is specifically indicated, select the agent, concentration and contact time for the wound and product. Historical examples include 0.25% sodium hypochlorite and 10% povidone-iodine containing 1% available iodine. Irrigation at 4–15 psi can remove debris. Avoid cytotoxic antiseptics on clean granulating tissue (pp692–693, 697; WHS guideline).

highlightAliases.old: Stage 3: full-thickness with fat visible, no exposed bone/muscle/tendon.
highlightAliases.new: Stage 3: full-thickness with fat visible, no exposed bone/muscle/tendon (p686-687, Figure 46-1).

highlightAliases.old: Exception: for clean wounds, less force and physiologic solutions such as normal saline can be used (p693), and antiseptics are avoided on clean and healing PI (p697).
highlightAliases.new: Exception: for clean wounds, less force and physiologic solutions such as normal saline can be used (p693), and povidone-iodine, iodophor, sodium hypochlorite, hydrogen peroxide, and acetic acid are avoided on clean and healing PI (p697).

highlightAliases.old: General turning interval q2–3h (p683); RCT of 942 NH residents randomized to q2h/q3h/q4h turning (p683) found no significant difference in PI incidence: 2.5% vs 0.6% vs 3.1% (p684).
highlightAliases.new: General turning interval q2–3h (p683); RCT of 942 NH residents on high-density foam mattresses randomized to q2h/q3h/q4h turning (p683) found no significant difference in PI incidence: 2.5% vs 0.6% vs 3.1% (p684).

highlightAliases.old: Thermography: cooler blanchable erythema predicts necrotic ulcer within 7 days; capacitance devices read in 3–8 seconds (p686).
highlightAliases.new: Thermography: in one NH study, areas of blanchable erythema with cooler skin temperatures were more likely to develop necrotic ulcers within 7 days; capacitance devices read in 3–8 seconds (p686).

highlightAliases.old: Parenteral empiric: cefazolin, ceftriaxone, clindamycin; vancomycin for MRSA; metronidazole/carbapenem/beta-lactamase inhibitor for anaerobes (p697).
highlightAliases.new: Parenteral empiric: cefazolin, ceftriaxone, clindamycin; vancomycin may be required for MRSA; metronidazole/carbapenem/beta-lactamase inhibitor for anaerobes (p697).

highlightAliases.old: In the RCT of 942 nursing home residents, did turning every 2, 3, or 4 hours change PI incidence significantly?
highlightAliases.new: In the RCT of 942 nursing home residents on high-density foam mattresses, did turning every 2, 3, or 4 hours change PI incidence significantly?

highlightAliases.old: No — 2.5% (q2h) vs 0.6% (q3h) vs 3.1% (q4h), not significantly different (p684).
highlightAliases.new: No — among residents on high-density foam mattresses, 2.5% (q2h) vs 0.6% (q3h) vs 3.1% (q4h), not significantly different (p684).

highlightAliases.new: PUSH scores wound area 0–10 (zero for a closed wound plus ten positive-size bands), exudate 0–3, and tissue type 0–4 (p689; NPIAP PUSH Tool 3.0).

highlightAliases.old: Saline/water lack antiseptic properties and should seldom be used on (colonized) PI — antiseptic options: Dakin's 0.25% or povidone-iodine (10%/1% free iodine) on colonized PI, applied 10–15 min before redressing; lavage 4–15 psi (p692). For clean wounds, less force and physiologic solutions such as normal saline can be used (p693); avoid povidone-iodine, iodophor, sodium hypochlorite, hydrogen peroxide, and acetic acid on clean and healing PI (p697).
highlightAliases.new: Clean a pressure injury with a nonirritating, nontoxic solution such as saline or clean water. Wound colonization alone does not justify routine antiseptics. If an antimicrobial cleanser is specifically indicated, select the agent, concentration and contact time for the wound and product. Historical examples include 0.25% sodium hypochlorite and 10% povidone-iodine containing 1% available iodine. Irrigation at 4–15 psi can remove debris. Avoid cytotoxic antiseptics on clean granulating tissue (pp692–693, 697; WHS guideline).
